findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL storage, snapshots and backups unencrypted, so any access to the underlying storage layer or a shared snapshot exposes the data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance an internet-routable endpoint (also exported as a Terraform output), exposing the database directly to untrusted networks and to brute-force/credential attacks against the 'admin' master user.

The master username is hard-coded to the default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a Terraform variable, so it is written in cleartext to Terraform state and is re-interpolated into EC2 user data. Combined with the public endpoint this is a direct credential-attack path.

The user_data script writes the database username and var.password in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF, is visible in the console, and is stored in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available. An SSRF in the PHP application on this host could retrieve the plaintext user-data secrets and the instance profile credentials for the wildcard IAM role.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is specified, so the instance volumes holding the plaintext credential include file may be stored unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to a role attached to an internet-reachable web instance, so any application compromise yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege escalation via role/instance manipulation and RDS master password reset.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, permitting unconstrained outbound connectivity that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; the PHP client in user_data uses mysqli_connect without TLS, sending credentials and query data in cleartext.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC has network-level access to the database; this weak segmentation compounds the publicly accessible endpoint.
